scope: Fixture strategies for data-driven Words LowCode types: MailMerger, Processor, ReportBuilder

strategy_for_data_driven_types.approach: All three types use programmatic DOCX creation via Aspose.Words Document+DocumentBuilder. No static fixture files from the GitHub repo are required. The LLM generates C# code that (1) creates the template/input DOCX programmatically, (2) calls the LowCode API, (3) validates the output.

template_docx_creation.mechanism: Document + DocumentBuilder C# API calls embedded in Program.cs before the LowCode API call
template_docx_creation.precedent: Already proven for Converter, Watermarker, Splitter, Replacer, Merger, Comparer. All 6 Wave 1+2 types use this pattern successfully (POST_MERGE_VERIFIED).
template_docx_creation.words_yml_key: template_hints.input_creation_lines (existing) and new family-specific keys for template-based types

merge_field_injection.mechanism: DocumentBuilder.InsertField() with FieldType.FieldMergeField or raw field code string
merge_field_injection.alternative_pattern: builder.InsertField(FieldType.FieldMergeField, false); (requires Aspose.Words.Fields namespace — use string form to minimize namespace imports)
merge_field_injection.field_name_coupling: The field names used in InsertField() MUST exactly match the string[] passed as fieldNames to MailMerger.Execute(). This is the critical coupling constraint the LLM must respect.

linq_tag_injection.mechanism: DocumentBuilder.Write() with literal LINQ Reporting Engine tag text
linq_tag_injection.syntax_note: LINQ Reporting Engine uses <<[Expression]>> delimiters. The text inside is a C# expression evaluated against the data object. For simple field access: <<[Name]>> accesses data.Name.
forbidden_formats: MERGEFIELD FieldName — mail merge field syntax
linq_tag_injection.data_coupling: The expression inside <<[...]>> must be a valid property or field access on the data object. For anonymous object new { Name = "World" }, the tag <<[Name]>> is correct.

MailMerger.rationale: Simplest Execute() overload. No IMailMergeDataSource needed. No DataRow/DataTable needed. String arrays are self-documenting in example code.

Processor.pattern: No data source — Processor converts a document from one format to another
Processor.rationale: Processor is a format converter, not a data-filling operation. Input is a plain DOCX. No data coupling required.

ReportBuilder.rationale: Anonymous objects are the simplest possible data source for LINQ Reporting Engine. They avoid POCO class definitions, DataTable setup, and XML/JSON parsing.
avoided_patterns: Named POCO class definitions requiring separate class files

inline_implementation.MailMerger: No custom class needed. Use string array overload: MailMerger.Execute(template, output, new[] { "FirstName", "LastName" }, new object[] { "John", "Doe" })
inline_implementation.Processor: No custom class needed. Fluent chain: new Processor().From(input).To(output, SaveFormat.Pdf).Execute()
inline_implementation.ReportBuilder: No custom class needed. Anonymous object: ReportBuilder.BuildReport(template, output, new { Name = "World" })

fixture_gaps.gap_description: words.yml template_hints is missing mail_merger_template_creation_lines. Without this, the LLM will not know to create a template DOCX with MERGEFIELD codes before calling MailMerger.Execute().
fixture_gaps.severity: BLOCKING — example will fail to compile or produce wrong output without the template
fixture_gaps.resolution: Add mail_merger_template_creation_lines to template_hints in words.yml

fixture_gaps.gap_description: words.yml template_hints has no entry for mail_merger_field_names or mail_merger_field_values. LLM may generate arbitrary field names that do not match the template.
fixture_gaps.severity: HIGH — field name mismatch between template and Execute() call causes silent failure (fields not filled, no exception)
fixture_gaps.resolution: Add explicit field name and value arrays to template_hints

fixture_gaps.gap_description: per_type_constraints.MailMerger is missing from words.yml. No constraints currently enforce LowCode API use or template field coupling.
per_type_constraints.Processor is missing from words.yml. LLM may confuse Processor with Converter and use static Converter.Convert() instead of the fluent Processor chain.
fixture_gaps.severity: MEDIUM — example may produce valid output but use wrong API
fixture_gaps.resolution: Add per_type_constraints.Processor block with fluent chain REQUIRED constraint

fixture_gaps.gap_description: Processor has no explicit constructors in the DLL catalog (constructors: []). The planner may classify it as non-runnable if constructor absence is interpreted strictly.
fixture_gaps.severity: LOW — classification already notes 'default constructor assumed' and standalone_allowed=true
fixture_gaps.resolution: Verify at generation time that new Processor() compiles. Monitor for build error. Classification confidence 0.85 is acceptable.
fixture_gaps.monitoring_action: Check build output after first pilot run. If 'Processor does not contain a constructor that takes 0 arguments' error appears, investigate Processor.Create() factory as alternative instantiation.

fixture_gaps.gap_description: words.yml template_hints is missing report_builder_template_creation_lines. Without LINQ tag injection instructions, LLM will not generate <<[Name]>> syntax in template creation code.
fixture_gaps.severity: BLOCKING — template without LINQ tags causes BuildReport() to output unmodified template; validation will fail

fixture_gaps.gap_description: per_type_constraints.ReportBuilder is missing from words.yml. LLM does not know the required <<[FieldName]>> LINQ tag syntax and may substitute MERGEFIELD or other syntax.
fixture_gaps.severity: HIGH — wrong syntax causes BuildReport() to leave tags unreplaced or throw MissingMember exception
fixture_gaps.resolution: Add per_type_constraints.ReportBuilder with explicit LINQ tag format constraint

fixture_gaps.gap_description: None of MailMerger, Processor, ReportBuilder are in words.yml allowed_types. Pipeline will block them at the allowlist gate before any code generation occurs.
fixture_gaps.severity: HARD BLOCK — scenario never reaches LLM
fixture_gaps.resolution: Add all three to allowed_types in words.yml after human APPROVE_EXPANSION authorization

template_hints_to_add.report_builder_linq_syntax_note: LINQ Reporting Engine uses <<[FieldName]>> tag syntax. Tags are replaced with matching data object property values during BuildReport().

required: REQUIRED: MailMerger.Execute(templateFile, outputFile, fieldNames, fieldValues) — static call
REQUIRED: template DOCX must contain MERGEFIELD fields matching fieldNames array (use DocumentBuilder.InsertField("MERGEFIELD FieldName"))
REQUIRED: fieldNames string array must match MERGEFIELD names exactly in the template DOCX
forbidden: FORBIDDEN: Document.MailMerge.Execute() replacing MailMerger.Execute() — use LowCode MailMerger
FORBIDDEN: IMailMergeDataSource implementation — use string/object array overload
FORBIDDEN: MailMergeDataSource.Create() in main scenario code

required: REQUIRED: new Processor().From(inputFile).To(outputFile, SaveFormat.Pdf).Execute() — fluent instance chain
REQUIRED: Processor is instantiated with new Processor() — NOT a static call
forbidden: FORBIDDEN: Document.Save() replacing Processor fluent chain — use LowCode Processor
FORBIDDEN: Processor.Convert() or Processor.Process() — primary operation is Execute() after From().To() chain

required: REQUIRED: ReportBuilder.BuildReport(templateFile, outputFile, dataObject) — static call
REQUIRED: template DOCX must contain LINQ Reporting Engine tags in <<[FieldName]>> syntax (e.g. <<[Name]>>)
REQUIRED: data object property names must match LINQ tag field names exactly
REQUIRED: template DOCX created programmatically via DocumentBuilder.Write() with literal LINQ tag text
forbidden: FORBIDDEN: ReportingEngine.BuildReport() — core API; use LowCode ReportBuilder.BuildReport()
FORBIDDEN: {FieldName} or {{FieldName}} or [FieldName] syntax — LINQ Reporting Engine requires <<[FieldName]>> format
FORBIDDEN: MERGEFIELD syntax in ReportBuilder template — that is MailMerger syntax

recommended_implementation_order.rationale: Lowest complexity. No new template fixture — reuses existing single-DOCX programmatic input pattern. No field coupling. Fluent API pattern is the only new concept. High confidence of first-pass LLM success.
recommended_implementation_order.prerequisite: Add Processor to allowed_types and per_type_constraints.Processor to words.yml

recommended_implementation_order.rationale: MERGEFIELD syntax is well-known to LLMs (standard Word mail merge). The programmatic InsertField() pattern is straightforward. Field name coupling is the main risk, mitigated by explicit constraints. Low-medium confidence of first-pass success.
recommended_implementation_order.prerequisite: Add MailMerger to allowed_types, mail_merger_template_creation_lines to template_hints, and per_type_constraints.MailMerger to words.yml. Close followup-words-mail-merger-fixture-documentation.

recommended_implementation_order.rationale: LINQ Reporting Engine <<[FieldName]>> syntax is less well-known than MERGEFIELD. Medium risk of LLM substituting wrong syntax. However, with explicit few-shot constraint injection, first-pass success is achievable.
recommended_implementation_order.prerequisite: Add ReportBuilder to allowed_types, report_builder_template_creation_lines to template_hints, and per_type_constraints.ReportBuilder to words.yml.
recommended_implementation_order.repair_strategy: If LLM uses wrong tag syntax, repair prompt should include explicit: 'CORRECTION: LINQ Reporting Engine requires <<[FieldName]>> syntax. You wrote {FieldName} which is wrong. Replace with <<[Name]>>.'
recommended_implementation_order.reviewer_note: Example reviewer should flag any DOCX output where the LINQ tags were NOT replaced (output still contains '<<') as a validation failure.

MailMerger.secondary: Open output DOCX with Aspose.Words.Document; read body text; verify 'John' and 'Doe' appear in body text
MailMerger.anti_check: Verify 'MERGEFIELD' string does NOT appear in body text (unreplaced fields indicate merge failure)
MailMerger.implementation_note: Use Aspose.Words Document.GetText() or NodeCollection traversal to read body text

Processor.implementation_note: Same as existing Converter output validator — can reuse pdf_header_check

ReportBuilder.secondary: Open output DOCX with Aspose.Words.Document; read body text; verify 'World' appears (from <<[Name]>> = 'World')
ReportBuilder.anti_check: Verify '<<' string does NOT appear in body text (unreplaced LINQ tags indicate template processing failure)
ReportBuilder.implementation_note: Use Aspose.Words Document.GetText() or NodeCollection traversal
